causes: 42 U.S.C. § 1983 — Denial of an impartial adjudicator (procedural due process)
42 U.S.C. § 1983 — Denial of a fair hearing (procedural due process)
Declaratory relief — 28 U.S.C. §§ 2201–2202 (vacatur of APS Decision 34739340)
Injunctive / Ex parte Young relief vs. DMV Director Gordon (official capacity)
key_facts: On November 1, 2024, CHP Officers Meza-Gonzalez and Melano contacted Plaintiff on the I-580 East shoulder in Livermore (CHP Case RJ68845). The DS-367 chemical-test-refusal designation and Arrest Report triggered DMV APS Case 34739340. After a January 24, 2025 Microsoft Teams hearing, Hearing Officer Diana Candelaria issued a February 11, 2025 Decision sustaining a one-year Class A CDL suspension (Feb. 20, 2025 – Feb. 19, 2026) without addressing the November 5, 2024 PC § 849(b)(1) Detention Certificate. Matter 7 (federal §1983, 2:26-cv-00983-DC-CSK) and Matter 8 (state mandate, 26WM000135, abandoned) litigate that APS outcome. This matter consolidates the underlying incident/APS evidence and both Candelaria docket PDF sets under one owning folder. Plaintiff signed an operative N.D. Cal. Complaint (v3, 47 pp.) and print intake packet against Candelaria (individual) and Gordon (official capacity) on Aug. 7, 2026, expressly alleging that the prior E.D. Cal. Matter 7 action arising from the same Nov. 1, 2024 incident was voluntarily dismissed without prejudice. The court docketed it as Dkt. 1 on Aug. 10, 2026. The court-stamped operative FAC is Dkt. 6 (filed Aug. 17, 2026, 44 pp.); Dkt. 5 (filed Aug. 14, 46 pp.) is the earlier stamped FAC. The unsigned Aug. 11 draft (Burrell v. Jackson removed) is retained as superseded. The FAC pleads that Plaintiff's SR-22 filing under Vehicle Code § 16430 became effective May 18, 2026 — a Dairyland/Viking non-owner policy at $281.28 per year — so the three-year maintenance period runs through approximately May 2029; Matter 32's ¶36(d) states the same end date for the same obligation. Drafts v1 (47 pp.) and v2 (15 pp. short-form) retained.
procedural_status: Opened August 7, 2026 as Matter 33 to hold the Candelaria / DMV APS slice of the CHP cluster: six Nov. 1 incident and APS discovery PDFs plus the Centerline wage reference in matter-33/incident/; twelve Matter 7 federal PDFs in matter-33/from-07/; six Matter 8 mandamus PDFs in matter-33/from-08/; and the June 15, 2026 Candelaria F&R in matter-33/opinions/. Matters 1, 2, 7, 8 and 32 cross-reference those paths. The N.D. Cal. complaint was signed Aug. 7 and docketed Aug. 10, 2026 as No. 3:26-cv-08272-LJC, assigned to Magistrate Judge Lisa J. Cisneros in San Francisco; the clerk's intake stamp shows the San Jose office. Four documents are on the docket: complaint (Dkt. 1), summonses as to both defendants (Dkt. 2), Plaintiff's magistrate-jurisdiction election consenting under 28 U.S.C. § 636(c) (Dkt. 3), and the court's order setting the initial case management conference and ADR deadlines (Dkt. 4). Both summonses are addressed to the defendants care of the DMV Legal Affairs Division, Mail Station C128, 2415 First Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95818. Candelaria and Gordon were personally served there Aug. 14, 2026 via the Sacramento County Sheriff, satisfying Rule 4(m) (had run to Nov. 8, 2026) and setting the answer/Rule 12 motion deadline at Sep. 4, 2026 (FRCP 12(a)(1)(A)(i)). FAC filings: Dkt. 5 First Amended Complaint (CONFORMED, filed Aug. 14, 2026, 46 pp.) and Dkt. 6 First Amended Complaint (CONFORMED, filed Aug. 17, 2026, 44 pp.) — Dkt. 6 is the operative court pleading of record (Burrell v. Jackson omitted; SR-22 through approximately May 2029). The unsigned Aug. 11 draft and the Aug. 10 FAC are superseded. Open items: the Civil L.R. 3-15 certification of conflicts and interested entities was due with Plaintiff's first appearance; an executed Sep. 4, 2026 Certification (Civil L.R. 3-15(c)(3) no-conflict form) is ready to file and is not yet on the docket; Dkt. 4 requires that order and the Civil L.R. 4-2 supplementary material to be served with the operative pleading; the § 636(c) consent binds only Plaintiff until both defendants consent, and a single declination reassigns the case to a district judge; the FAC still identifies the related Meza-Gonzalez action by caption only, so its case number (3:26-cv-08271-PHK) must be inserted at ¶¶ 8, 14, 31 and 88. Related case listed on the JS-44: Serrato 4:26-cv-05953-ASK. Dated deadlines live in timeline.json. Dkt. 9 (FILED Aug. 26, 2026) is the clerk-stamped Proof of Service that Dkt. 6 was mailed first-class from San Jose on Aug. 21, 2026 to both defendants at DMV Legal Affairs C128. That mailing is Rule 5 service of the amended pleading, not a new Rule 4 start date. On September 8, 2026 Mag. Krishnan declined to relate this action to Serrato (Candelaria Dkt. 13 / Serrato Dkt. 23); the case stays with Mag. Cisneros. PACER Sep. 9, 2026 (2 pp., $0.20) shows the docket through Dkt. 14: Dkt. 7 summons returned executed (Candelaria and Gordon served Aug. 14, answer due Sep. 4); Dkt. 8 administrative motion to relate (filed Aug. 25); Dkt. 9 POS of the FAC (filed Aug. 26); Dkt. 10 Notice Identifying Operative FAC (filed Aug. 26, entered Aug. 27 — stamped PDF not yet pulled); Dkt. 11 Answer (Sep. 4) lists Rob Bonta, Attorney General; Fiel Dizon Tigno, Supervising Deputy Attorney General; and William J. McMahon, Deputy Attorney General (SBN 178588), who signed. PACER names Tigno lead counsel / attorney to be noticed for both defendants (1515 Clay Street, 20th Floor, P.O. Box 70550, Oakland, CA 94612-0550; (510) 622-2214; fiel.tigno@doj.ca.gov). Dkt. 12 (Sep. 8, text-only) requires defendants to file a consent or declination to magistrate-judge jurisdiction by September 22, 2026. Dkt. 14 (Sep. 8, modified the same day) is a second clerk's notice filed in the wrong case — DISREGARD; the live clock is Dkt. 12. Plaintiff's Civil L.R. 3-15 certification remains executed Sep. 4 and is still not on this docket.
damages: The Dkt. 1 complaint seeks compensatory damages exceeding $214,000, punitive damages of at least $100,000, JS-44 demand alignment $250,000 (min.), vacatur of APS Case 34739340, SR-22 relief, CDL-record expungement, and structural APS reform. Matter 33 also remains documentary owner of the Matter 7/8 PDF sets (no separate damages under the document-home role).
risk: Refiled in N.D. Cal. before the Matter 7 E.D. Cal. voluntary dismissal was actually filed; CONFIRMED Aug. 15, 2026 that the dismissal Dkt. 1 represented to this court is now on the E.D. Cal. docket. Watch claim-preclusion and forum-shopping arguments given the gap between the Aug. 10 refile and the Aug. 15 dismissal. Service is CONFIRMED complete: Candelaria and Gordon were personally served Aug. 14, 2026 through DMV Legal Affairs in Sacramento, satisfying Rule 4(m) (had run to Nov. 8, 2026) and starting the Sep. 4, 2026 answer/Rule 12 motion clock. The Aug. 21 first-class mailing of Dkt. 6 (Dkt. 9 POS, filed Aug. 26) does not restart that clock. Consenting to magistrate jurisdiction gives up the district-judge review layer that produced the Matter 7 objections track, and is ineffective unless both defendants also consent. Dkt. 11 answered rather than declined; Dkt. 12 now sets defendants' magistrate consent/declination for Sep. 22, 2026 — a single declination still reassigns the case. Dkt. 1 carries a known-fabricated authority at page 43: Burrell v. Jackson, 2003 WL 23545858, which the citation ledger records as NOT_FOUND. A nonexistent case cannot be distinguished, and the defendants would brief quasi-judicial immunity straight at that passage. The First Amended Complaint cures it — neither Burrell nor its companion cite (Baker v. Bzdyra, 2019 WL 6619348, misspelled 'Bzydra' in Dkt. 1) appears anywhere in the FAC. Dkt. 6 (filed Aug. 17, 2026) is now the pleading of record; retire the citation debt once downstream indexes catch up. Coordinate with the Matter 32 Meza-Gonzalez N.D. Cal. companion (No. 3:26-cv-08271-PHK, also served Aug. 14, 2026) and the Serrato related-case notice. Path updates for Matters 1/2/7/8/32 already point at /documents/matter-33/ for the historical PDF set.
